html:
Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom of the English Midlands, centred on the River Trent. It is on the map for 800 and 900, and for much of the 700s it was the strongest kingdom in England.

Its pagan king Penda beat the Northumbrians repeatedly in the 600s. Its greatest king, Offa, ruled from 757 to 796. He controlled London and Kent, minted silver pennies in large numbers, dealt with Charlemagne as an equal, and built Offa's Dyke against the Welsh.

In 825 Mercia lost to Wessex and never recovered its lead. In 873 to 874 the Great Heathen Army drove its king from Repton and split the kingdom. The western half was ruled by Æthelred and then by Æthelflæd, Lady of the Mercians, daughter of Alfred the Great. After her death in 918 it was absorbed into Wessex.
sum: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom of the English Midlands, centred on the River Trent. It is on the map for 800 and 900, and for much of the 700s it was the strongest kingdom in England.
